comparison: Both evaluate the crystal structure and crosslinking strategy (C4-C7, C51-C56, C93, C97). OpenEval finds the structural evidence SUPPORTED with ~2800 Å² buried surface area and specific interactions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, acknowledging it as 'a key advance' but expressing concern that 'the crosslink stabilizes an usually underpopulated conformation' and requesting additional validation, placing 'a significant burden of proof' on the authors.

Both evaluate the acidic loop mechanism claims (C75-C82). Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the mutagenesis is clear but mechanistic interpretation relies on computational modeling of an invisible loop. Peer reviewers explicitly criticize the detailed modeling as 'more appropriate for a high-resolution crystal structure' and state 'a more qualitative model would have sufficed,' indicating the mechanistic claims are overinterpreted.

Both evaluate substrate selection and linker length requirements (C88-C92, C107). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the systematic testing and ~25 Å distance providing structural rationale. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the finding, stating the structure 'places steric constraints' consistent with biochemical analysis showing inefficient ubiquitylation when lysine is too close to the WW docking site.

Both evaluate mutagenesis mapping functional regions (C58-C62, C68-C70). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing selective defects, yeast complementation, and convergent evidence. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, describing 'convincing evidence' and 'nice confirmation' through 'multiple approaches.' OpenEval R3 focuses on specific mutations (R74A, S774A, F806A) while peer R2 includes broader interface mutagenesis (C49-C50, C64-C66).

Both address alanine scanning and interface mutagenesis. OpenEval R2 evaluates C47, C49-C50, C64-C66 as SUPPORTED, emphasizing pulse-chase assays and interface mutations. Peer R2 covers overlapping claims (C49-C50, C64-C66) plus additional mutations (C58-C63, C68-C70) and rates SUPPORTED. The peer review encompasses a broader set of mutagenesis data in their positive evaluation.

Both evaluate conservation and generality across NEDD4-family members (C84, C86-C87). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing polyubiquitination, cross-species validation, and sequence conservation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging conservation and common architecture (C111), though they note 'somewhat different results' between assay types, suggesting minor reservations about complete generality.

Both evaluate integration with prior E2~Ub-HECT structures and conformational changes (C94-C96). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing systematic mutagenesis validation and the ~130° rotation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, positively describing the 'dramatic conformational change' and integration with Schulman lab work, noting the model of switching between two states is well-supported.

Both address the minimal Rsp5WW3-HECT construct validation (C47). OpenEval rates the construct as SUPPORTED and functional. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether mutations 'disrupt interactions with the C-lobe...rather than with MBP' in the fusion protein assay, noting different assays 'seemed to give somewhat different results' and requesting clarification about what the data actually report.

Both address mechanistic comparisons between HECT and RING E3s (C99, C104). OpenEval R11 rates SUPPORTED, noting structural data supports distinct mechanisms. Peer R6 also rates SUPPORTED in the context of conformational changes and integration with prior work. Limited overlap (2 claims) but both positive about the comparative mechanistic conclusions.

Both touch on common architecture for substrate and Ub-to-Ub ligation (C111). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic proposals about C-lobe rotation are speculative inferences requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED overall for conservation/generality claims but acknowledge 'somewhat different results' between substrate types, suggesting partial alignment on this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates the acidic C-terminus role (C71-C74) as UNCERTAIN due to conflicting deletion versus substitution data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about the C-terminus.

OpenEval rates extensive background literature claims (C1-C3, C8-C30, C36-C46) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide necessary context but are not novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel claims rather than cataloging background citations.

OpenEval rates claims about prior knowledge gaps and motivating hypotheses (C15-C16, C33-C35, C48) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent framing of the research question rather than testable claims.
OpenEval rates citations to prior work on lysine selection by RING E3s (C105-C106) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative context claims from other studies.
